message.content:
The corpus addresses MTPD setting mainly through the BIA workflow. There, the MTPD comes out of a structured interview with the activity owner: the interview takes impacts over time first, then the MTPD, then the resource requirements in their four classes, then the dependencies. The approvals are placed with the activity owner, who approves the data and sets MTPD and RTO — so the number is the owner's call, not the AI's. The owner sets the recovery fields, and stage 4 is only accepted when impacts over time are evidenced and the owner has set them.

Two related points. First, the guidance treats impact categories, time horizons and thresholds as method parameters: they are agreed and supplied before stage 1 runs, and no stage of the workflow sets them — so AI supports the collection and recording of the MTPD but never determines it. Second, the outcome of a BIA is a list of requirements, and a requirement names what an activity needs in order to run; it does not assert that the thing exists today. The consolidated results still need checking, and top management approves the BIA results before solutions design starts.

The glossary defines MTPD as how long an activity can be down before the impact is unacceptable, but the excerpts don't give a method for arriving at the figure beyond the interview sequence above, nor guidance on MTPD setting outside the BIA workflow.
